title: Pick a Character Trait to Work On
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Starting from the idea that character shapes a person's trajectory, the article argues that leaders can deliberately strengthen character one trait at a time. It suggests beginning with an inventory of traits essential for success, offering a list that includes patience, humility, courage and discipline. No one masters all traits, so the goal is steady improvement on a single trait over several months. The author recommends seeking situations that test the chosen trait, experimenting with new approaches and keeping a journal of progress and setbacks. After taking stock, the leader picks another trait. The piece closes with a Heraclitus quotation that good character is built little by little through patient effort.
points: Character is framed as an inner resource that grows stronger or weaker with each task and challenge.
The method is to focus on one trait for several months rather than attempting to master everything.
Deliberately seeking situations that test the chosen trait, such as tasks that try patience, provides practice.
A journal of progress and setbacks turns character work into a tracked discipline.
quotes: The strength of a person’s character is an inner resource developed through experience, commitment, and personal values. Character grows stronger or weaker with each task and challenge people face.

Purposely working to strengthen one’s character is not as difficult as people think. Improving character begins with an inventory of the character traits you view as essential for success, both professionally and personally.

No one has mastered all of the traits, nor will they in a lifetime. That’s not the goal. The key for leaders is to make steady improvement on one trait at a time, strengthening their character through focus, reflection, and practice.

Seek opportunities to put the trait into action both mindfully and purposely. For instance, let’s say you want to work on patience to strengthen your character. Look for tasks and episodes that will try your patience.

Stay with this for an extended period of time. Keep a journal of your experiences, noting the progress you have made and the setbacks you have encountered. This is the blocking and tackling of character work.
In the words of Heraclitus, “Good character is not formed in a week or a month. It is created little by little, day by day. Protracted and patient effort is needed to develop good character.
